name: Chrome Gospel: Verses from the Wired Saints
creator: Edited by Kofi Brandt-Vasquez
description: An anthology of 63 poets from the Gray Zone and Tier 2 underground scene, all writing about augmentation from the perspective of those who had no choice — military-grade chrome from debt-indenture contracts, forced medical implants from corponation insurance schemes, black-market geneware gone wrong. The anthology is organized liturgically, with sections titled Wounds, Consecration, Testimony, and Reckoning, and the editorial framing argues explicitly that involuntary augmentation is a form of bodily colonization. Physical copies are hand-assembled in rotating locations across the Gray Zone.
medium: physical zine-anthology (rotating print collective) and encrypted pirate neural feed
cultural_impact: Gave literary form and community to the involuntary augmentation survivor movement; the phrase 'wired saint' has become a term of solidarity and reclamation among the Gray Zone communities.
controversy: Three of the poets included were subsequently targeted by corponation IP enforcement for publishing content that referenced proprietary augmentation hardware in ways deemed defamatory; the editor, Brandt-Vasquez, has been detained twice.
story_hooks: One of the 63 poets has disappeared, and the poem attributed to them in the anthology contains what appears to be an encoded location — but no one who has tried to decode it agrees on the method.
A Tier 4 literary award committee wants to nominate Chrome Gospel, and the editorial collective is violently divided on whether accepting would be cooptation or leverage.
A corponation has begun quietly buying up every physical copy it can locate — not for legal reasons, but because a senior executive was named in one of the poems.
